If the old migrated profile is not accessible or deleted by you. It's possible your old mac was using a a different version of Thunderbird. You did not mention what version you were using on the old mac.

No worries, you just create a new gmail imap account and it will show everything that is lurking on the server - as viewed via webmail account. As you mention gmail, I suggest you check a few things first and then proceed to create the mail account.

Check this:

Firewall: Make sure Thunderbird program is set up as an allowed program

VPN: Gmail does not like VPN, so check computer and switch it off. Some Anti-Virus apps auto provide and enable VPNs.

Localhost: Some people use programs like 'Apache' to eg: maintain websites. It's important to switch those programs off until Oauth2 token has been set up.

In Thunderbird check this:

  • Settings > Privacy & Security
  • select 'Accept cookies from sites'
  • click on 'Exceptions' button
  • Enter : https://accounts.google.com
  • click on 'Allow'
  • click on 'Save Changes'

Then whilst in 'Privacy & Security' section

  • check the 'Passwords' section
  • Click on 'Saved Passwords'
  • if you see any mention of gmail possibly from a previous install then remove all lines to do with gmail.

Create the mail account

  • Menu app icon > New Account > Email
  • Enter name, email address and password

Password is the same password you use to access webmail account

  • Remember password' should be selected
  • click on Continue

By default Thunderbird will look for the IMAP settings.

You will then get a prompt by google to enter email address and password because gmail is checking you really are you , then you say to allow Thunderbird access to server.

Gmail sets up an Oauth token which gets saved in same are as passwords. Thunderbird then uses that token to access server.

content:
Two possibilities: - the install is corrupted. download thunderbird again and install over the top of the failing one - OR, the profile is corrupt, in which case you can still import messages after restarting with a clean profile. To do that, here are suggested steps:

  1. copy the profile with the messages you want away from the thunderbird profile to ensure it is safe
  2. delete the ...appdata\roaming\thunderbird folder
  3. restart thunderbird, which will then create a new profile
  4. setup account normally
  5. now , to salvage to old messages, do this:
    • install the importexporttools NG addon
    • highlight Local Folders and rightclick
    • select the importexport option to import mbox file '
    • locate and select one of the desired message folders from old profile. these will appear in sets, such as inbox, inbox.msf, sent, sent.msf, etc. ignore the msf entries, as the other file is the one with the messages.
    • repeat the process for each message folder to import

content:
You cannot compare sending emails via webmail because it's not using the same protocols. One is direct from the server the other needs to access the server in order to use its imap and smtp server settings.

The error message is from the server not Thunderbird.

Error message of that type tend to be created because and not limited to:

  • an authentication issue
  • a block due to a server Spam filter failure
  • VPN enabled

First check your computer to see if a VPN has been enabled. Many Anti-Virus products now include a VPN and in some cases the AV can auto enable it. Switch VPN off. The VPN will hide your IP address, so server may think you are not you and block all attempts to access server.


Check the authentication method being used.

It would be helpful to know what server settings are being used. Please upload images that show:

  1. Account settings > 'Server Settings' for the account
  2. Account Settings > 'Outgoing Server(SMTP)' (located at bottom of left pane) - then select the smtp being used.

I presume you are using Imap so server settings to use: IMAP

  • Incoming server: imap.videotron.ca
  • Port : 993
  • Connection Security: SSL/TLS
  • User name: full email address
  • Authentication Method: Normal Password
  • Password: same one you use to access webmail account

SMTP:

  • Outgoing server: smtp.videotron.ca
  • Port : 465
  • Connection Security: SSL/TLS
  • User name: full email address
  • Authentication Method: Normal Password
  • Password: same one you use to access webmail account

IMAP

Passwords can be checked in this location:

  • Settings > Privacy & Security
  • scroll down to 'Passwords' section
  • click on 'Saved Passwords'
  • click on 'Show Passwords'

You should see two line for each mail account/email address. One is incoming and the other outgoing. To Edit a stored password:

  • Right click on each line in turn and select 'Edit Password'
  • Completely clear the stored password and then carefully type the correct password
  • Click on 'Close' when finished.

Note the password should be exactly the same as used to access webmail account. If you update/change password - Exit Thunderbird, wait a few moments for background processes to complete then restart Thunderbird.
